# Energy balance with direct use (Phase 4E upgrade)

*Generated by `python -m solvia.pipeline --steps energy_balance`. All solar figures are ESTIMATES.*

Method: monthly kWp × NASA POWER GHI × performance ratio 0.75; each day is split into 96 blocks with the measured solar output shape (healthy Kaggle inverters, 81% of their energy falls in 09:00–16:00) and the measured eMARC load shape of the household type. Direct use = Σ min(solar, load); the rest of the solar is exported, the rest of the load comes from the grid. No battery.

## Example: a typical Pune home of each type, sized to cover its yearly use (rounded up to 0.5 kWp)

| household_type | daily_use_kwh | kwp | solar_kwh | consumption_kwh | direct_use_kwh | export_kwh | grid_import_kwh | self_sufficiency_pct | self_consumption_pct |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Basic | 3.94 | 1.5 | 2083.7 | 1440.6 | 595.5 | 1488.2 | 845.1 | 41.3 | 28.6 |
| Water Heaters but no AC | 4.65 | 1.5 | 2083.7 | 1699.0 | 805.2 | 1278.5 | 893.8 | 47.4 | 38.6 |
| With Air Conditioners | 5.79 | 2.0 | 2778.3 | 2115.5 | 909.4 | 1869.0 | 1206.1 | 43.0 | 32.7 |

kWh per year. `self_sufficiency_pct` = share of the home's use covered directly by its panels; `self_consumption_pct` = share of the panels' output used in the home.

- Solar output is an ESTIMATE: kWp × long-term NASA POWER irradiance × performance ratio, not a measurement.
- Real savings depend on when you use electricity (solar is produced in daytime only), net-metering rules and tariffs.
- Range shows a typical poor month (10th percentile) to a typical good month (90th percentile) of 2001–2025.
- Direct use (solar used at the moment it is produced) combines the measured 15-minute shape of the Kaggle plants' output (southern India, May–June) with the measured eMARC load shape of the household type; it is an estimate for an average day, not a simulation of each day.
